title: VPC ingress backpressure + tenant-aware local buffering for on-prem observability
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Enable robust ingress flow-control and local spool buffering for Dedicated and Private (VPC / on-prem) observability collectors. This ticket implements a signaling protocol and local tenant-aware storage layer so relays can gracefully shed load, persist telemetry when upstream is congested, and replay when capacity returns. It covers tracing hook propagation for sampling decisions, metrics and log pipeline tagging for tenant isolation, disk spool encryption, and dashboarding requirements for latency/error SLOs in private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Collectors respond with structured backpressure signals (HTTP 429 + X-RW-Backpressure-Token + Retry-After) when their in-memory pipeline surpasses thresholds
Relays maintain per-tenant token-bucket limits and drop-low-priority logs/traces first according to tenant QoS policy
Local spool persists up to configured bytes per tenant (default 5GB), encrypted-at-rest, and replays in FIFO order when upstream reports healthy
Tracing hooks propagate sampling & priority headers (X-RW-Trace-Sample, X-RW-Trace-Priority) through relays so sampling decisions remain consistent end-to-end
Metrics emitted: ingress_queue_length, spool_bytes_used, per_tenant_drop_rate, backpressure_events, replay_rate, upstream_ok_ratio
Dashboard panels exist for Private/Dedicated SLOs: 99th p95/p99 ingress latency, per-tenant error rates, spool pressure heatmap, backpressure events timeline
Automated e2e test simulating upstream outage demonstrates no silent data-loss for tenants within spool quota and correct replay behavior
design_decisions: Use HTTP-based backpressure signalling (429 + custom headers) to remain compatible with existing forwarders and make it observable
Per-tenant token buckets are preferred over global caps to avoid noisy-neighbor amplification in multi-tenant relays
Local spool is append-only immutable segments with a sliding LRU eviction across tenants constrained by per-tenant quotas
Encryption: use customer-provided KMS key when available; fallback to service-managed envelope keys for hosted Dedicated
Tracing headers defined as namespaced X-RW-* to avoid collision with external tooling and to simplify header inspection in dashboards
tasks: Spec: define header names, HTTP status semantics, and retry semantics (owner: Miguel)
Proto impl: add backpressure response path to relay ingress code (owner: Eng-Relay Team)
Buffering: implement per-tenant spool with disk-backed segments and encryption (owner: Storage Team)
Sampling hooks: propagate and persist trace sampling headers in span envelopes (owner: Tracing Team)
Metrics: add exporter metrics and OpenTelemetry semantic conventions mapping (owner: Observability Team)
Dashboard: create dashboard template and panels for Private/Dedicated in Grafana (owner: Platform Observability)
E2E tests: inject synthetic upstream failure and verify replay behavior (owner: Test Automation)
Docs: runbook for operators covering spool tuning, emergency drain, and key rotation (owner: Docs)
Security review and threat model update (owner: Security), depends on security_review_required
notes: Tradeoffs: disk-spooling prevents short-term data loss but increases complexity for consistency and increases operator burden for key management
We considered gRPC flow control but standardized on HTTP for compatibility with existing customer relays and edge proxies
Target spool default per-tenant of 5GB balances typical production telemetry vs disk cost in on-prem appliances; we will expose this as runtime-configurable
Eviction policy: low-priority logs -> traces with low sampling -> metrics (last resort) to preserve core observability signals
Performance target: backpressure path must be activatable within 2ms of queue threshold crossing and add <0.5ms median latency when inactive
